To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
benthic nitrogen fixation in sediments of a Peruvian oxygen minimum is controlled by organic carbon availability and free sulfide.
N2 fixation and the potential coupling with SR were detected at all sites in sediments of Peruvian oxygen minimum zones.

N2 fixation was detected in all sediment samples of the Peruvian OM Z, with highest rates at the upper stations and lower rates at the deepest sites; N2 fixation and the SR process overlapped in all samples; and N2 fixation was positively related with organic matter and negatively related with free sulfide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential coupling of benthic N fixation and sulfate reduction in the sediments of the OMZ off Peru.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coupling of benthic N 2 fixation and SR is possible but not a general feature in the Peruvian oxygen-depleted zone.
N2 fixation is not a major process in the Peruvian oxygen-minimum zone, but that it can be important in certain locations.
N2 fixation in Peruvian OMZ sediment was not linked with SR, but rather with other processes, such as organic matter decomposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N2 fixation is not coupled to SR in sediments of this OMZ, but is controlled by organic carbon availability.
N2 fixation in Peruvian OMZ can be attributed to a variety of organisms, and that N2 fixation is coupled to organic matter mineralization, but not to sulfate reduction.
N2 fixation in sediments of OMZ is not a unique feature but a common phenomenon in organic-rich sediments of the world's oceans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
benthic diazotrophic activity in the OMZ sediments is mainly controlled by organic matter, while sulfate-reducing conditions are of secondary importance.
benthic nitrogen fixation in sediments of Peruvian OMZ can be coupled with SR.
benthic nitrogen fixation is a widespread process that can contribute to N2 fixation in sediments of oxygen minimum zones.
